extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in Hungarian politics and Wikipedia users
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the 2012 allegations that Ferenc Gyurcsány plagiarized his 1984 college thesis, including reported evidence, university records, media claims, and subsequent actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common errors and omissions as evidence of plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Hír TV located and compared the reviews of both works and found that based on the common errors and omissions, Gyurcsány's thesis is likely to be identical to the first half of Rozs's, supporting the allegations of plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matching uncommon errors or identical omissions in two works can be taken as supporting evidence of copying; however, the Wikipedia article notes that the original works themselves were not compared and the media outlet did not publish the materials, so such claims should be treated with caution until primary documents are available for independent verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and documentation of a submitted thesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Gyurcsány published a page from his course record book stating that he submitted and defended a college thesis, while the University of Pécs reported they were unable to find his diploma thesis and that it was the only missing work from that time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary evidence (e.g., university records, course books) that a thesis was submitted and defended is an important criterion for verifying the existence of the work; lack of a physical or archived copy complicates verification and invites additional investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct comparison of original works for conclusive findings
rubrics_metrics.description: The article observes that the original works, however, were not compared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A definitive determination of textual identity or plagiarism requires side-by-side comparison of the original documents. Analyses based only on secondary materials (e.g., reviews) are inherently limited and should note that limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and availability of evidentiary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Hír TV, which reported the findings, had not made any of the materials cited available to other media outlets for analysis as of 4 May 2012.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For credibility and independent verification, media outlets or investigators presenting evidence should release source materials (documents, scans, reviews) so that others can evaluate the claims; withholding materials undermines the strength of allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegations of theft and legal remedies affecting evidence access
rubrics_metrics.description: Gyurcsány filed a criminal complaint for the apparent theft of his thesis from the university, believed to have occurred during the media coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that a thesis was stolen or removed from archives impact the availability and chain of custody of evidence; pursuing legal remedies (e.g., criminal complaints) may be part of the process to recover documents or establish how materials went missing, but such actions also complicate timely independent verification.
